quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Look for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. They warn you and show you which way to go.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, you should:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross, even if there is no marked crosswalk.

questions.question: If a road is slippery, maintain a following distance that is:

options.text: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on slippery roads than on dry roads. Keep a larger space between you and the car ahead.

questions.question: You should not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses, due to their size and weight, require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.
Large trucks and buses travel at a higher speeds than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses, due to their size and weight, require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop than small cars. A sudden stop in front of them may cause a crash because the driver cannot stop in time.

questions.question: When in a vehicle, wear a seat belt:
questions.correctAnswerText: All the time.
questions.explanation: The law requires drivers and front seat passengers to always wear a seat belt. Anyone under 16 must wear a seat belt or use a child safety seat, no matter where they sit.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area designated for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are areas where pedestrians can cross the street. They are usually marked with white lines. Some crosswalks are not marked.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part does not protect you well. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: A driver who has been drinking is more likely to:

options.text: Keep a three to four second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a slower reaction time.
questions.explanation: Drinking impairs driving ability even below the legal limit. Just one drink can affect your vision, motor skills, and reaction time, which increases crash risk.

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, you should:

options.text: Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guards signals for you to go.
Be prepared to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: This five-sided sign means you are near a school. Be alert and stop if children are crossing.

questions.question: When driving in fog, it is best to drive with:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams bounce off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is a distraction because:

options.text: It makes the driver worry about the cost of the call.
It takes up the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.
It catches the attention of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes up the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous. It uses your eyes, hands, and mind. Even good drivers increase their crash risk when using a cell phone.

questions.question: In a vehicle with airbags, the safest place for children age 12 and under is:

options.text: The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags can be dangerous for children. Children age 12 and under should always sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: If pedestrians are crossing the street illegally instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they are crossing where they should not, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass.
questions.explanation: Alcohol leaves your system slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol level. The only way to reduce it is to wait.

questions.question: Driving under the influence of medication that impairs your driving is allowed:
questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that impairs your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross when the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Go if you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian crosses before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses before going.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must let any vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians in the intersection go first. Wait until the pedestrian has crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at a rest area to nap, stretch, or change drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks do not replace real rest and may make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or change drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid tired driving, take a break every hour on long trips. If possible, share driving with another person so you can both rest.

questions.question: When you see an octagonal sign, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means "Stop." Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, you become:
questions.correctAnswerText: More intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: A school bus uses flashing red lights and a stop arm when loading or unloading students. Do not move forward until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back in. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Your tires do not grip the road as well when it is wet, snowy, or icy. Slow down when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street:

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only have to yield the right-of-way at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians using a guide dog or carrying a white cane.

questions.question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your body. Eating, drinking coffee, or taking a shower will not speed this up.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:

options.text: Making sudden and unsafe lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making sudden and unsafe lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers while driving. If you see an aggressive driver making sudden or unsafe lane changes, do not confront them. The safest choice is to move out of their way.
